https://www.whitehousehistory.org/events.description: Save the date! The White House Historical Association will be hosting their annual Holiday Book Festival and Closeout Sale on December 4. Since 1962, the White House Historical Association has produced award-winning books on many subjects related to the history of the President's House—from its architecture, gardens, fine and decorative arts to the presidents and first ladies who lived there over the years. Our titles appeal to history buffs and art lovers, connoisseurs and curious amateurs, scholars and tourists, adults and children. We are pleased to invite you to meet the authors of these award-winning books at our Holiday Book Festival on December 4, 2026. Featured Authors: Leslie Greene Bowman will be signing her forthcoming title, to be released in October 2026, Art for the White House: A Changing Portrait of America . Author John Wrory Ficklin will be signing his new book An Unusual Path: Three Generations from Slavery to the White House . Former White House Chief Usher Gary Walters will be signing his new memoir White House Memories, 1970–2007: Recollections of the Longest Serving Chief Usher . Thomas Jefferson (as portrayed by historical actor-interpreter Bill Barker of Monticello), will greet the public and be available to sign his book, Becoming Jefferson . Bruce M. White , a fine art and architectural photographer, will be available to sign many White House Historical Association titles, of which he was principal photographer. Christina Ewald will sign articles written for White House HIstory Quarterly . Artist Peter Waddell will be available to speak about his paintings in progress and sign articles written for White House History Quarterly . Author Rocco Smirne will sign his latest release Rocco C elebrates America's 250th Birthday at the White House . With his fifth book on White House history, he takes us on a journey through the White House where 250 years of America’s history can be found in the halls and collections. More authors to be announced! RSVP Directions

https://www.whitehousehistory.org/events.description: Join Leslie Greene Bowman at the Barnes & Noble Georgetown for an author talk and book signing! About the Book Released in celebration of America's 250th year, Art for the White House: A Changing Portrait of America by Leslie Greene Bowman, presents a wholly new perspective on the White House fine arts collection, revealing how all two-hundred and fifty years of America’s history can be told through the collection. Bowman begins with the story of how the collection was created—slowly and cautiously—as our young nation was eager to distinguish itself from artwork that could be associated with the patronage and luxuries of European monarchs. Bowman continues her narrative thematically through more than two centuries of American history with chapters focused on “Independence Declared,” “The Way West,” “America the Beautiful,” “The Innovators,” and more. The richly illustrated chapters highlight examples from the collection by the greatest masters of American Art including Gilbert Stuart, Charles Bird King, Winslow Homer, Albert Bierstadt, Mary Cassatt, Georgia O'Keeffe, Jacob Lawrence, John Singer Sargent, Roy Lichtenstein and others. About the Author Leslie Greene Bowman is an author, historian, and president emerita of Thomas Jefferson’s Monticello in Charlottesville, Virginia. She has devoted her career to art and history museums. After serving as curator of decorative arts and assistant director of exhibitions at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, she was named director of Winterthur Museum, Garden and Library in Delaware in 1999. From 2008 to 2023 she was president of the Thomas Jefferson Foundation, which owns and operates Monticello. In addition to numerous articles, Bowman is author of American Arts and Crafts: Virtue in Design , and, with Morrison H. Heckscher, American Rococo, 1750–1775: Elegance in Ornament. She conceived and co-edited the examination of Jefferson’s impact on the arts in Thomas Jefferson at Monticello: Architecture, Landscape, Collections, Books, Food, Wine . Bowman earned her bachelor of philosophy degree at Miami University of Ohio and her master of arts degree in early American culture as a Winterthur Fellow at the University of Delaware. She is a trustee emerita of both the National Trust for Historic Preservation and the Association of Art Museum Directors. By presidential appointment, she served on the Committee for the Preservation of the White House under Presidents Biden, Trump, Obama, George W. Bush, and Clinton. Bowman lives in Keswick, Virginia, with her dogs and horses. She travels frequently, especially to Europe. Besides riding, she is fond of biking, hiking, cooking and new adventures. RSVP Directions

https://www.whitehousehistory.org/events.description: The White House Historical Association offers free public tours of historic Decatur House every Monday, excluding federal holidays and the Monday following Thanksgiving.* A fixture of the president’s neighborhood since 1818, Decatur House has been home to foreign and American dignitaries, secretaries of state, members of Congress, and a vice president, in addition to numerous free and enslaved servants who played a pivotal role in shaping America. Visit and explore the nearly 200-year history of Decatur House and its Slave Quarters, the only existing slave quarters within sight of the White House and learn more about the many additional programs and offerings of the Association. Tours begin at 1610 H Street, NW at 10:30am and 1pm and last approximately one hour. Visitors will be required to reserve their free spot on the tour via Eventbrite. If you’re looking to schedule a private Decatur House tour for your group Tuesday-Friday, please complete our private tour request form here . RSVP Here Directions Additional Information Nearby Parking Garages: 1625 I Street NW / 1750 H Street NW / 1050 Connecticut Avenue NW Nearest Metro Stops: Farragut West and McPherson Square on the Blue/Orange/Silver Line, and Farragut North on the Red Line

Location: David M. Rubenstein National Center for White House History at Decatur House

https://www.whitehousehistory.org/events.description: Join us in learning more about White House History right from your own home. Our Facebook Live series, White House History Live, delves into the stories that make up the history of the Executive Mansion. In our December episode, historian Dr. Denver Brunsman will join the program to discuss his new book: George Washington and His World . Dr. Brunsman provides a fresh perspective on the first president’s remarkable life by removing centuries of myth and highlighting the people and society around him that made his achievements possible. This virtual event will be streamed on the White House Historical Association’s Facebook and YouTube pages starting at 5:30 pm ET on December 8. Join Us on Facebook Directions

https://www.whitehousehistory.org/events.description: Join us in learning more about White House History right from your own home. Our Facebook Live series, White House History Live, delves into the stories that make up the history of the Executive Mansion. This October, the White House Historical Association launches a new digital project that tells the stories of over 1,000 men and women who have worked behind the scenes at the President’s House from 1789 to the present. From cooks and gardeners to coachmen and butlers, these workers are the people behind the People’s House. In this episode of White House History Live, join Association historians Lina Mann and Sarah Fling to learn more about this project and hear about five fascinating individuals who worked at the White House over the last two centuries. This virtual event will be live streamed on the White House Historical Association's Facebook and YouTube pages starting at 5:30 pm ET on October 20. Join Us on Facebook Directions
